newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end weaker with U.S. ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end weaker with U.S. ahead of data.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended weaker on Thursday, though spreads to U.S. bonds narrowed amid investor anxiety ahead of Friday's U.S. payrolls data, analysts said.

"People are just getting ready for tomorrow's payroll number," said Harv Kalirai, Canadian analyst with I.D.E.A. "A lot of players are worried about this number and the best hedge for a strong payrolls number is to play Canada-U.S. spreads. That's what's been going on today."
Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 fell C$0.25 to C$100.10 to yield 7.989 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 20/32 to yield 7.15 percent.
The spread between benchmark bonds narrowed to 84 basis points from 86 basis points at Wednesday's close.
Both Canadian and U.S. investors are looking ahead to the release on Friday of the U.S. non-farm payrolls report for August, seen as a key measure of U.S. economic growth.
Many are worried that a stronger-than-expected number could lead to higher U.S. interest rates.

Canadian and U.S. bond markets weakened this morning after a report that U.S. jobless claims for the week ended August 31 fell to 316,000 from 331,000 the previous week. Economists had forecast jobless claims of 335,000.
"You're just getting signs the U.S. economy is not slowing down. Canada obviously takes direction from the U.S., but still we're outperforming," said Kalirai.
In auction news, the government of Canada said it will hold seven bond auctions, including one real return issue, in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The first auction, of 10-year bonds, will be on September 18, with details to be released on September 12.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.13 to C$96.12 to yield 7.549 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 12/32 to yield 6.98 percent.
The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 57 basis points from 58 basis points at the close of trading on Thursday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 4.03 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.35 percent.
